invention.ref: Medieval shoes with laces through eyelets, 12th century (Museum of London)
invention.ref_zh: 12 世纪的中世纪鞋已用鞋带穿过鞋眼（伦敦博物馆）

patent.ref: Harvey Kennedy patents the aglet-tipped shoelace in the UK
patent.ref_zh: 肯尼迪在英国为带金属头的鞋带申请专利

notes: 更早的「鞋带」见于亚美尼亚 Areni-1 皮鞋（约前 3500 年）和冰人奥茨的鞋（约前 3300 年），早于本站年份范围；本条目以伦敦博物馆记录的 12 世纪鞋带作为现代意义鞋带的起点。
summary_zh: 12 世纪的中世纪鞋已用鞋带穿过鞋眼系紧；1790 年哈维·肯尼迪在英国为两端带硬头的鞋带申请了专利。
summary_en: Medieval shoes from the 12th century were already laced through eyelets; in 1790 Harvey Kennedy patented aglet-tipped shoelaces in the UK.
notes_en: Earlier laces appear on the Areni-1 shoe (c. 3500 BCE) and Ötzi's shoes (c. 3300 BCE), both before this atlas's year range. This entry starts with 12th-century laced shoes documented by the Museum of London.
